title: Nutty Chewy Ethiopian Teff Injera
description: A traditional Ethiopian flatbread with a nutty, chewy texture and a smoky flavor, made with teff flour, butter, and spices. Perfect for serving with stews or salads.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine teff flour, yeast, salt, smoked paprika, black pepper, and garlic powder. Mix well.
Gradually add water to the bowl, stirring with a wooden spoon until a smooth batter forms.
Add vegetable oil, xanthan gum (if using), and mix until well combined.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the mixture rest in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Heat a non-stick skillet or a traditional Ethiopian injera pan over medium heat.
Brush the pan with butter and pour 1/4 cup of the batter into the pan, tilting to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip the injera and cook for another 30 seconds to 1 minute, until it's lightly browned.
Repeat with the remaining batter, brushing the pan with butter between each injera.
Serve the injera hot, garnished with chopped cilantro leaves (if desired).
